definitions.explanation: A group or faction that advocates or uses extreme methods to achieve political or social goals. Can refer to violent political movements or more broadly to the extreme wing of any organization.

examples.japanese: {過激派|かげきは}による{犯行|はんこう}だと{報道|ほうどう}された。
examples.english: It was reported as an act by extremists.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}は{過激派|かげきは}の{取|と}り{締|し}まりを{強化|きょうか}した。
examples.english: The government strengthened its crackdown on extremists.

examples.japanese: {穏健|おんけん}な{改革|かいかく}を{求|もと}めるグループと{過激派|かげきは}の{間|あいだ}で{対立|たいりつ}が{深|ふか}まっている。
examples.english: The conflict is deepening between the group seeking moderate reform and the radicals.

notes:
A compound of {過激|かげき} (extreme, radical) and {派|は} (faction, school, group). The suffix {派|は} is productive and attaches to many words to indicate a faction or group.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {過激派|かげきは}グループ (extremist group)
- {過激派|かげきは}{組織|そしき} (extremist organization)
- {過激派|かげきは}の{活動|かつどう} (radical activities)
- {過激派|かげきは}による{犯行|はんこう} (crime by extremists)
- {過激派|かげきは}を{取|と}り{締|し}まる (to crack down on extremists)

In Japanese postwar history, {過激派|かげきは} often refers to the radical student movements ({学生|がくせい}{運動|うんどう}) of the 1960s-70s. In modern usage, it is also used for international extremist groups. The opposite concept is {穏健派|おんけんは} (moderates).
